topic: A person learns their favorite restaurant is closing
text: I hear the old mill's to shut its doors, same as the tale you've spun 'bout your favorite eatery. Folk gather, and I watch their sorrow, a shadow on the village sun. I can only think on the wheat that goes unground, the work left undone, like the meals now made scarce. I know I should tend the fields, my hands in the earth, but a part of me feels the weight of change, a shift in the air, as if the heavens themselves hold their breath. I’ll say a prayer, perhaps the good saints will grant a favor, turn the course of what ails us all. But for now, I must return to the soil, to the tasks that keep this world turning, even as parts of it fall still.
